from pathlib import Path
import os
import re

from dotenv import load_dotenv
from pymongo import MongoClient


# ============================================================
# CONFIGURATION
# ============================================================

BASE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent

# Your backend uses server/.env
ENV_FILE = BASE_DIR.parent.parent / "server" / ".env"

load_dotenv(ENV_FILE)

MONGO_URI = os.getenv("MONGO_URI")

if not MONGO_URI:
    raise RuntimeError(
        "MONGO_URI not found in server/.env"
    )


DATABASE_NAME = "test"

SOURCE_COLLECTION = "experiences"

TARGET_COLLECTION = "experiencechunks"


# ============================================================
# CHUNK CONFIGURATION
# ============================================================

# Approximate character size.
#
# 1 token is roughly 4 characters for normal English text.
#
# 3000 characters ≈ 750 tokens.
#
# We keep chunks reasonably small so retrieval can return
# focused portions of an interview experience.

CHUNK_SIZE = 3000

# Overlap prevents important information from being cut
# exactly at a chunk boundary.

CHUNK_OVERLAP = 300


# ============================================================
# TEXT CLEANING
# ============================================================

def clean_text(text):
    """
    Clean extracted interview text while preserving
    paragraph structure.
    """

    if not text:
        return ""

    # Normalize Windows line endings.
    text = text.replace("\r\n", "\n")

    # Replace tabs with spaces.
    text = text.replace("\t", " ")

    # Remove excessive spaces.
    text = re.sub(
        r"[ ]{2,}",
        " ",
        text
    )

    # Collapse excessive blank lines.
    text = re.sub(
        r"\n{3,}",
        "\n\n",
        text
    )

    return text.strip()


# ============================================================
# CHUNKING
# ============================================================

def split_text(text):
    """
    Split text into chunks while trying to respect
    paragraph and sentence boundaries.
    """

    text = clean_text(text)

    if not text:
        return []

    chunks = []

    start = 0

    text_length = len(text)

    while start < text_length:

        end = min(
            start + CHUNK_SIZE,
            text_length
        )

        # If this isn't the last chunk,
        # try to move the boundary to a natural
        # paragraph/sentence boundary.

        if end < text_length:

            # Look for a paragraph break.
            paragraph_boundary = text.rfind(
                "\n\n",
                start,
                end
            )

            # If no paragraph boundary,
            # look for a sentence boundary.
            sentence_boundary = text.rfind(
                ". ",
                start,
                end
            )

            # Prefer paragraph boundary.
            if paragraph_boundary > start + CHUNK_SIZE // 2:

                end = paragraph_boundary + 2

            elif sentence_boundary > start + CHUNK_SIZE // 2:

                end = sentence_boundary + 2

        chunk = text[start:end].strip()

        if chunk:
            chunks.append(chunk)

        # Last chunk.
        if end >= text_length:
            break

        # Move backwards by overlap.
        start = end - CHUNK_OVERLAP

        if start < 0:
            start = 0

    return chunks


# ============================================================
# CONNECT TO MONGODB
# ============================================================

print()
print("=" * 60)
print("INTERVJTI EXPERIENCE CHUNKING")
print("=" * 60)

print("Connecting to MongoDB...")

client = MongoClient(MONGO_URI)

# Test connection.
client.admin.command("ping")

db = client[DATABASE_NAME]

experiences = db[SOURCE_COLLECTION]

chunks_collection = db[TARGET_COLLECTION]

print(
    f"Connected to database: {DATABASE_NAME}"
)

print(
    f"Experiences found: "
    f"{experiences.count_documents({})}"
)


# ============================================================
# CLEAR EXISTING CHUNKS
# ============================================================

# We want this script to be safely re-runnable.
#
# For development, we'll remove previously generated
# chunks and rebuild them.

print()
print("Removing previous generated chunks...")

delete_result = chunks_collection.delete_many({})

print(
    f"Deleted {delete_result.deleted_count} "
    f"old chunks."
)


# ============================================================
# PROCESS EXPERIENCES
# ============================================================

total_experiences = experiences.count_documents({})

total_chunks = 0

failed = 0


cursor = experiences.find({})


for index, experience in enumerate(
    cursor,
    start=1
):

    experience_id = experience["_id"]

    student_name = experience.get(
        "studentName",
        "Unknown"
    )

    company_name = experience.get(
        "companyName",
        "Unknown"
    )

    content = experience.get(
        "content",
        ""
    )

    source = experience.get(
        "source",
        {}
    )

    print()
    print(
        f"[{index}/{total_experiences}] "
        f"{student_name} - {company_name}"
    )


    try:

        chunks = split_text(content)

        if not chunks:

            print(
                "  SKIPPED: no usable content"
            )

            continue


        documents = []


        for chunk_index, chunk_text in enumerate(
            chunks
        ):

            document = {

                "experienceId": experience_id,

                "chunkIndex": chunk_index,

                "text": chunk_text,

                "companyName": company_name,

                "year": source.get(
                    "year"
                ),

                "experienceType": source.get(
                    "experienceType"
                ),

                "studentName": student_name,

                "source": {

                    "fileId": source.get(
                        "fileId"
                    ),

                    "fileName": source.get(
                        "fileName"
                    ),

                    "originalPath": source.get(
                        "originalPath"
                    )

                }

            }

            documents.append(
                document
            )


        if documents:

            result = chunks_collection.insert_many(
                documents
            )

            count = len(
                result.inserted_ids
            )

            total_chunks += count

            print(
                f"  Created {count} chunks"
            )


    except Exception as error:

        failed += 1

        print(
            f"  FAILED: {error}"
        )


# ============================================================
# SUMMARY
# ============================================================

print()
print("=" * 60)
print("CHUNKING COMPLETE")
print("=" * 60)

print(
    f"Experiences processed : "
    f"{total_experiences}"
)

print(
    f"Chunks created        : "
    f"{total_chunks}"
)

print(
    f"Failed experiences    : "
    f"{failed}"
)

print("=" * 60)


client.close()

print(
    "MongoDB connection closed."
)

from pathlib import Path
import os
import time

from dotenv import load_dotenv
from pymongo import MongoClient
from google import genai
from google.genai import types


# ============================================================
# CONFIGURATION
# ============================================================

BASE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent

# server/.env
ENV_FILE = BASE_DIR.parent.parent / "server" / ".env"

# Load both:
# - GEMINI_API_KEY
# - MONGO_URI
load_dotenv(ENV_FILE)


GEMINI_API_KEY = os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY")
MONGO_URI = os.getenv("MONGO_URI")

if not GEMINI_API_KEY:
    raise RuntimeError(
        "GEMINI_API_KEY was not found in server/.env"
    )

if not MONGO_URI:
    raise RuntimeError(
        "MONGO_URI was not found in server/.env"
    )


DATABASE_NAME = "test"

COLLECTION_NAME = "experiencechunks"

MODEL_NAME = "gemini-embedding-001"


# ============================================================
# EMBEDDING CONFIGURATION
# ============================================================

# We use 768 dimensions.
#
# Gemini allows configurable output dimensionality for newer
# embedding models. Keeping this at 768 makes the vectors
# smaller while remaining useful for semantic retrieval.
#
# IMPORTANT:
# The same dimensionality MUST be used later when embedding
# the user's query.

OUTPUT_DIMENSIONALITY = 768


# ============================================================
# RETRY CONFIGURATION
# ============================================================

MAX_RETRIES = 5

INITIAL_RETRY_DELAY = 5


# ============================================================
# CREATE GEMINI CLIENT
# ============================================================

gemini_client = genai.Client(
    api_key=GEMINI_API_KEY
)


# ============================================================
# EMBEDDING FUNCTION
# ============================================================

def generate_embedding(text):
    """
    Generate one embedding vector using Gemini.
    """

    for attempt in range(1, MAX_RETRIES + 1):

        try:

            response = gemini_client.models.embed_content(

                model=MODEL_NAME,

                contents=text,

                config=types.EmbedContentConfig(

                    output_dimensionality=OUTPUT_DIMENSIONALITY,

                    task_type="RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT"

                )
            )

            if not response.embeddings:

                raise RuntimeError(
                    "Gemini returned no embeddings."
                )

            embedding = response.embeddings[0].values

            if not embedding:

                raise RuntimeError(
                    "Gemini returned an empty embedding."
                )

            return embedding


        except Exception as error:

            print(
                f"    Embedding attempt "
                f"{attempt}/{MAX_RETRIES} failed:"
            )

            print(
                f"    {error}"
            )

            if attempt == MAX_RETRIES:

                raise


            delay = INITIAL_RETRY_DELAY * (
                2 ** (attempt - 1)
            )

            print(
                f"    Retrying in {delay} seconds..."
            )

            time.sleep(delay)


# ============================================================
# CONNECT TO MONGODB
# ============================================================

print()
print("=" * 60)
print("INTERVJTI GEMINI EMBEDDING GENERATION")
print("=" * 60)

print("Connecting to MongoDB...")


mongo_client = MongoClient(
    MONGO_URI
)

# Test connection.
mongo_client.admin.command("ping")


db = mongo_client[
    DATABASE_NAME
]

collection = db[
    COLLECTION_NAME
]


print(
    f"Connected to database: "
    f"{DATABASE_NAME}"
)

print(
    f"Collection: "
    f"{COLLECTION_NAME}"
)


# ============================================================
# COUNT CHUNKS
# ============================================================

total_chunks = collection.count_documents({})

embedded_chunks = collection.count_documents(
    {
        "embedding": {
            "$exists": True,
            "$ne": None
        }
    }
)

remaining_chunks = (
    total_chunks - embedded_chunks
)


print()
print(
    f"Total chunks      : {total_chunks}"
)

print(
    f"Already embedded  : {embedded_chunks}"
)

print(
    f"Remaining         : {remaining_chunks}"
)


# ============================================================
# SAFETY CHECK
# ============================================================

if total_chunks == 0:

    print()
    print(
        "No chunks found."
    )

    print(
        "Run chunk.py first."
    )

    mongo_client.close()

    raise SystemExit


if remaining_chunks == 0:

    print()
    print(
        "All chunks already have embeddings."
    )

    print(
        "Nothing to do."
    )

    mongo_client.close()

    raise SystemExit


# ============================================================
# PROCESS CHUNKS
# ============================================================

print()
print(
    "Starting embedding generation..."
)

print(
    "Model:",
    MODEL_NAME
)

print(
    "Dimensions:",
    OUTPUT_DIMENSIONALITY
)

print()


cursor = collection.find(
    {
        "$or": [
            {
                "embedding": {
                    "$exists": False
                }
            },
            {
                "embedding": None
            }
        ]
    },
    {
        "_id": 1,
        "text": 1,
        "companyName": 1,
        "studentName": 1,
        "chunkIndex": 1
    }
)


successful = 0
failed = 0


for index, chunk in enumerate(
    cursor,
    start=1
):

    chunk_id = chunk["_id"]

    text = chunk.get(
        "text",
        ""
    )

    company = chunk.get(
        "companyName",
        "Unknown"
    )

    student = chunk.get(
        "studentName",
        "Unknown"
    )

    chunk_index = chunk.get(
        "chunkIndex",
        0
    )


    print(
        f"[{index}/{remaining_chunks}] "
        f"{company} | "
        f"{student} | "
        f"chunk {chunk_index}"
    )


    if not text.strip():

        print(
            "    SKIPPED: empty text"
        )

        failed += 1

        continue


    try:

        embedding = generate_embedding(
            text
        )


        # Store embedding in MongoDB.
        collection.update_one(

            {
                "_id": chunk_id
            },

            {
                "$set": {
                    "embedding": embedding
                }
            }
        )


        successful += 1


        print(
            f"    SUCCESS "
            f"({len(embedding)} dimensions)"
        )


    except Exception as error:

        failed += 1

        print(
            f"    FAILED: {error}"
        )


# ============================================================
# FINAL VERIFICATION
# ============================================================

final_embedded = collection.count_documents(
    {
        "embedding": {
            "$exists": True,
            "$ne": None
        }
    }
)


print()
print("=" * 60)
print("EMBEDDING COMPLETE")
print("=" * 60)

print(
    f"Total chunks       : {total_chunks}"
)

print(
    f"Successful         : {successful}"
)

print(
    f"Failed             : {failed}"
)

print(
    f"Total with vectors : {final_embedded}"
)

print(
    f"Vector dimensions  : {OUTPUT_DIMENSIONALITY}"
)

print("=" * 60)


mongo_client.close()

print(
    "MongoDB connection closed."
)

FILE: ai\ingestion\extract.py

from pathlib import Path
import json
import hashlib
import pymupdf


# ============================================================
# PATHS
# ============================================================

BASE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent

# Root directory containing the original PDF collection
PDF_ROOT = Path(
    r"C:\Users\shivk\Downloads\Internship Guide - CoC"
)

OUTPUT_DIR = BASE_DIR / "output"

OUTPUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)


# ============================================================
# GENERATE STABLE FILE ID
# ============================================================

def generate_file_id(file_path: Path) -> str:
    """
    Generate a stable ID based on the PDF contents.

    Same PDF content = same ID.
    """

    sha256 = hashlib.sha256()

    with open(file_path, "rb") as file:

        while chunk := file.read(1024 * 1024):
            sha256.update(chunk)

    return sha256.hexdigest()[:16]


# ============================================================
# EXTRACT METADATA FROM PATH
# ============================================================

def extract_path_metadata(file_path: Path):
    """
    Extract useful metadata from the folder structure.

    Example:

    2025 Experiences/
        Internships/
            BNY/
                rushi bny 2025.pdf

    becomes:

    year = 2025
    experienceType = Internships
    companyFolder = BNY
    """

    relative_path = file_path.relative_to(PDF_ROOT)

    parts = relative_path.parts

    metadata = {
        "originalPath": str(relative_path),
        "year": None,
        "experienceType": None,
        "companyFolder": None
    }

    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Find the "Experiences" folder
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    experience_folder_index = None

    for index, part in enumerate(parts):

        if part.endswith("Experiences"):
            experience_folder_index = index
            break

    if experience_folder_index is not None:

        experience_folder = parts[experience_folder_index]

        # Example:
        # "2025 Experiences" -> "2025"

        if experience_folder[:4].isdigit():
            metadata["year"] = experience_folder[:4]

        elif experience_folder.lower().startswith("pre"):
            metadata["year"] = "pre-2018"


        # ----------------------------------------------------
        # Folder immediately after Experiences
        # ----------------------------------------------------

        type_index = experience_folder_index + 1

        if type_index < len(parts) - 1:
            metadata["experienceType"] = parts[type_index]


        # ----------------------------------------------------
        # Folder immediately before PDF
        # ----------------------------------------------------

        if len(parts) >= 2:

            company_folder = parts[-2]

            metadata["companyFolder"] = company_folder

    return metadata


# ============================================================
# EXTRACT ONE PDF
# ============================================================

def extract_pdf(file_path: Path):

    print(f"Processing: {file_path}")

    file_id = generate_file_id(file_path)

    output_file = OUTPUT_DIR / f"{file_id}.json"


    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Skip if already successfully processed
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    if output_file.exists():

        try:

            with open(output_file, "r", encoding="utf-8") as file:
                existing_data = json.load(file)

            if existing_data.get("status") == "success":

                print(
                    f"SKIPPED: {file_path.name} "
                    f"(already processed)"
                )

                return existing_data

        except Exception:
            pass


    try:

        # ----------------------------------------------------
        # Metadata
        # ----------------------------------------------------

        path_metadata = extract_path_metadata(file_path)


        # ----------------------------------------------------
        # Open PDF
        # ----------------------------------------------------

        document = pymupdf.open(file_path)

        pages = []


        # ----------------------------------------------------
        # Extract every page
        # ----------------------------------------------------

        for page_number, page in enumerate(
            document,
            start=1
        ):

            text = page.get_text("text").strip()

            pages.append({
                "pageNumber": page_number,
                "text": text
            })


        document.close()


        # ----------------------------------------------------
        # Check extracted text
        # ----------------------------------------------------

        total_text_length = sum(
            len(page["text"])
            for page in pages
        )


        if total_text_length < 100:

            status = "ocr_required"

            print(
                f"WARNING: {file_path.name} "
                f"contains very little extractable text."
            )

        else:

            status = "success"

            print(
                f"SUCCESS: {file_path.name} "
                f"({len(pages)} pages)"
            )


        # ----------------------------------------------------
        # Final result
        # ----------------------------------------------------

        result = {

            "fileId": file_id,

            "fileName": file_path.name,

            "status": status,

            "source": path_metadata,

            "pages": pages
        }


        # ----------------------------------------------------
        # Save
        # ----------------------------------------------------

        with open(
            output_file,
            "w",
            encoding="utf-8"
        ) as file:

            json.dump(
                result,
                file,
                ensure_ascii=False,
                indent=2
            )


        return result


    except Exception as error:

        print(
            f"FAILED: {file_path.name}"
        )

        print(
            f"Error: {error}"
        )


        result = {

            "fileId": file_id,

            "fileName": file_path.name,

            "status": "failed",

            "source": extract_path_metadata(file_path),

            "error": str(error),

            "pages": []
        }


        with open(
            output_file,
            "w",
            encoding="utf-8"
        ) as file:

            json.dump(
                result,
                file,
                ensure_ascii=False,
                indent=2
            )


        return result


# ============================================================
# FIND RELEVANT PDFs
# ============================================================

def find_experience_pdfs():

    pdf_files = []

    for pdf_file in PDF_ROOT.rglob("*.pdf"):

        relative_path = pdf_file.relative_to(PDF_ROOT)

        # Check whether this PDF is somewhere inside
        # a folder whose name ends with "Experiences".

        if any(
            part.endswith("Experiences")
            for part in relative_path.parts
        ):

            pdf_files.append(pdf_file)


    return sorted(pdf_files)


# ============================================================
# MAIN
# ============================================================

def main():

    if not PDF_ROOT.exists():

        raise RuntimeError(
            f"PDF root directory does not exist:\n"
            f"{PDF_ROOT}"
        )


    pdf_files = find_experience_pdfs()


    print("=" * 60)
    print("INTERVJTI PDF INGESTION")
    print("=" * 60)

    print(
        f"PDF root: {PDF_ROOT}"
    )

    print(
        f"Found {len(pdf_files)} experience PDF(s)."
    )

    print("=" * 60)
    print()


    successful = 0
    ocr_required = 0
    failed = 0
    skipped = 0


    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Process files
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    for index, pdf_file in enumerate(
        pdf_files,
        start=1
    ):

        print(
            f"[{index}/{len(pdf_files)}]"
        )

        result = extract_pdf(pdf_file)


        if result is None:
            failed += 1

        elif result["status"] == "success":

            # Determine whether this was newly processed
            output_file = OUTPUT_DIR / (
                f"{result['fileId']}.json"
            )

            # We count it as processed here.
            successful += 1

        elif result["status"] == "ocr_required":

            ocr_required += 1

        elif result["status"] == "failed":

            failed += 1


        print()


    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Final report
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    print("=" * 60)
    print("INGESTION COMPLETE")
    print("=" * 60)

    print(
        f"Total PDFs       : {len(pdf_files)}"
    )

    print(
        f"Successful       : {successful}"
    )

    print(
        f"OCR required     : {ocr_required}"
    )

    print(
        f"Failed           : {failed}"
    )

    print("=" * 60)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

from pathlib import Path
import json
import os

from dotenv import load_dotenv
from pymongo import MongoClient
from bson import ObjectId


# ============================================================
# PATHS
# ============================================================

BASE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent

STRUCTURED_DIR = BASE_DIR / "structured"


# ============================================================
# LOAD ENVIRONMENT
# ============================================================

# Your backend uses MONGO_URI.
#
# We will first look in the backend .env,
# then fall back to ai/ingestion/.env.

BACKEND_ENV = BASE_DIR.parent.parent / "server" / ".env"

LOCAL_ENV = BASE_DIR / ".env"


if BACKEND_ENV.exists():

    load_dotenv(
        BACKEND_ENV
    )

else:

    load_dotenv(
        LOCAL_ENV
    )


MONGO_URI = os.getenv(
    "MONGO_URI"
)


if not MONGO_URI:

    raise RuntimeError(
        "MONGO_URI was not found.\n\n"
        "Your backend uses process.env.MONGO_URI.\n"
        "Make sure server/.env contains MONGO_URI."

# ============================================================
# IMPORT CONFIGURATION

# ============================================================

    "Connecting to MongoDB..."

json_files = sorted(

if not json_files:

    print(
        "No structured JSON files found."

    client.close()

    raise SystemExit(0)


# ============================================================
# COUNTERS
# ============================================================

imported = 0

skipped = 0

failed = 0


# ============================================================
# PROCESS FILE
# ============================================================

for index, json_file in enumerate(
    json_files,
    start=1
):

    print()
    print(
        f"[{index}/{len(json_files)}] "
        f"{json_file.name}"
    )


    try:

        # ----------------------------------------------------
        # Load JSON
        # ----------------------------------------------------

        with open(
            json_file,
            "r",
            encoding="utf-8"
        ) as file:

            data = json.load(
                file
            )


        # ----------------------------------------------------
        # Basic validation
        # ----------------------------------------------------

        required_fields = [

            "studentName",

            "companyName",

            "batch",

            "preview",

            "content"

        ]


        missing_fields = [

            field

            for field in required_fields

            if field not in data

        ]


        if missing_fields:

            raise ValueError(

                "Missing fields: "
                + ", ".join(
                    missing_fields
                )

            )


        # ----------------------------------------------------
        # Get source metadata
        # ----------------------------------------------------

        source = data.get(
            "source",
            {}
        )


        file_id = source.get(
            "fileId"
        )


        if not file_id:

            # Fall back to JSON filename.

            file_id = json_file.stem


        # ----------------------------------------------------
        # DUPLICATE CHECK
        # ----------------------------------------------------

        existing = experiences_collection.find_one(

            {
                "source.fileId": file_id
            }

        )


        if existing:

            print(
                "SKIPPED: already exists in MongoDB"
            )

            skipped += 1

            continue


        # ----------------------------------------------------
        # Build Experience document
        # ----------------------------------------------------

        experience = {

            "userId": system_user_id,

            "studentName": data.get(
                "studentName",
                "Not specified"
            ),

            "companyName": data.get(
                "companyName",
                "Not specified"
            ),

            "batch": data.get(
                "batch",
                "Not specified"
            ),

            "preview": data.get(
                "preview",
                ""
            ),

            "content": data.get(
                "content",
                ""
            ),

            # Imported historical experiences
            # should be immediately available.

            "status": "approved",

            "source": {

                "fileId": file_id,

                "fileName": source.get(
                    "fileName"
                ),

                "originalPath": source.get(
                    "originalPath"
                ),

                "year": source.get(
                    "year"
                ),

                "experienceType": source.get(
                    "experienceType"
                ),

                "companyFolder": source.get(
                    "companyFolder"
                )

            },

            # Keep compatibility with your
            # existing schema field.

            "importSourcePath": source.get(
                "originalPath"
            )

        }


        # ----------------------------------------------------
        # Insert
        # ----------------------------------------------------

        result = experiences_collection.insert_one(
            experience
        )


        print(
            f"IMPORTED: {result.inserted_id}"
        )


        imported += 1


    except Exception as error:

        failed += 1


        print(
            f"FAILED: {json_file.name}"
        )

        print(
            f"Error: {error}"
        )


# ============================================================
# FINAL SUMMARY
# ============================================================

print()
print("=" * 60)
print("IMPORT COMPLETE")
print("=" * 60)

print(
    f"JSON files : {len(json_files)}"
)

print(
    f"Imported   : {imported}"
)

    f"Skipped    : {skipped}"
)

    f"Failed     : {failed}"
)

============================================================
FILE: ai\ingestion\structure.py

from pathlib import Path
import json
import os
import time
from datetime import datetime

from dotenv import load_dotenv
from google import genai


# ============================================================
# PATHS
# ============================================================

BASE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent

# Extracted PDF JSON files
INPUT_DIR = BASE_DIR / "output"

# Successfully structured files
STRUCTURED_DIR = BASE_DIR / "structured"

# Failed processing information
FAILED_DIR = BASE_DIR / "failed"

STRUCTURED_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
FAILED_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)


# ============================================================
# GEMINI CONFIGURATION
# ============================================================

load_dotenv(BASE_DIR / ".env")

api_key = os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY")

if not api_key:
    raise RuntimeError(
        "GEMINI_API_KEY was not found.\n"
        "Make sure ai/ingestion/.env exists and contains:\n"
        "GEMINI_API_KEY=your_key_here"
    )

client = genai.Client(api_key=api_key)

MODEL = "gemini-3.5-flash-lite"


# ============================================================
# GEMINI OUTPUT SCHEMA
# ============================================================

EXPERIENCE_SCHEMA = {
    "type": "object",

    "properties": {

        "studentName": {
            "type": "string"
        },

        "companyName": {
            "type": "string"
        },

        "batch": {
            "type": "string"
        },

        "preview": {
            "type": "string"
        },

        "content": {
            "type": "string"
        }
    },

    "required": [
        "studentName",
        "companyName",
        "batch",
        "preview",
        "content"
    ]
}


# ============================================================
# LOAD JSON
# ============================================================

def load_json(file_path):

    with open(
        file_path,
        "r",
        encoding="utf-8"
    ) as file:

        return json.load(file)


# ============================================================
# BUILD DOCUMENT TEXT
# ============================================================

def build_document_text(data):

    pages = data.get("pages", [])

    sections = []

    for page in pages:

        text = page.get(
            "text",
            ""
        ).strip()

        if not text:
            continue

        page_number = page.get(
            "pageNumber",
            "?"
        )

        sections.append(
            f"--- PAGE {page_number} ---\n"
            f"{text}"
        )

    return "\n\n".join(sections)


# ============================================================
# EXTRACT STRUCTURED EXPERIENCE USING GEMINI
# ============================================================

def extract_experience(data):

    document_text = build_document_text(data)

    source = data.get(
        "source",
        {}
    )

    source_year = source.get(
        "year",
        "Not specified"
    )

    source_type = source.get(
        "experienceType",
        "Not specified"
    )

    source_company = source.get(
        "companyFolder",
        "Not specified"
    )


    prompt = f"""
You are an information extraction system for Intervjti,
an interview-experience platform.

Your task is to convert the supplied interview-experience
document into the required JSON structure.

IMPORTANT RULES:

1. ONLY use information explicitly present in the document
   or the supplied source metadata.

2. NEVER invent information.

3. NEVER use outside knowledge.

4. If the student's name cannot be determined,
   return:

   "Not specified"

5. If the batch cannot be determined,
   return:

   "Not specified"

6. Do NOT infer a batch from the year.

7. The company folder supplied in the metadata is:

   {source_company}

   Use it as the company name when it clearly represents
   the company associated with the experience.

8. Do NOT invent or guess a company name.

9. The "content" field must preserve the COMPLETE
   interview experience.

10. DO NOT summarize the content field.

11. Preserve meaningful details such as:

    - Online assessments
    - Coding questions
    - Interview rounds
    - Technical questions
    - DSA questions
    - OOP questions
    - DBMS
    - Operating Systems
    - Computer Networks
    - System Design
    - Projects
    - Technologies
    - Cloud
    - HR questions
    - Behavioral questions
    - Interviewer's comments
    - Candidate's comments
    - Final result
    - Preparation advice
    - Resources
    - Important tips

12. You may clean obvious PDF extraction problems such as:

    - Excessive whitespace
    - Broken line formatting
    - Repeated line breaks

13. Do NOT remove meaningful information.

14. The "preview" field should be a concise 1-2 sentence
    description of the experience.

15. If information is unavailable, use:

    "Not specified"

SOURCE METADATA

Year:
{source_year}

Experience Type:
{source_type}

Company Folder:
{source_company}


SOURCE DOCUMENT

{document_text}
"""


    response = client.models.generate_content(

        model=MODEL,

        contents=prompt,

        config={
            "response_mime_type": "application/json",
            "response_schema": EXPERIENCE_SCHEMA
        }
    )


    return json.loads(
        response.text
    )


# ============================================================
# VALIDATE OUTPUT
# ============================================================

def validate_experience(data):

    required_fields = [
        "studentName",
        "companyName",
        "batch",
        "preview",
        "content"
    ]

    for field in required_fields:

        if field not in data:

            return (
                False,
                f"Missing field: {field}"
            )


        if not isinstance(
            data[field],
            str
        ):

            return (
                False,
                f"Invalid type: {field}"
            )


        if not data[field].strip():

            return (
                False,
                f"Empty field: {field}"
            )


    return True, None


# ============================================================
# SAVE FAILURE INFORMATION
# ============================================================

def save_failure(
    json_file,
    error
):

    failure_file = (
        FAILED_DIR /
        f"{json_file.stem}.json"
    )


    result = {

        "fileId": json_file.stem,

        "inputFile": json_file.name,

        "error": str(error),

        "timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat()
    }


    with open(
        failure_file,
        "w",
        encoding="utf-8"
    ) as file:

        json.dump(
            result,
            file,
            ensure_ascii=False,
            indent=2
        )


# ============================================================
# PROCESS ONE FILE
# ============================================================

def process_file(json_file):

    output_file = (
        STRUCTURED_DIR /
        json_file.name
    )


    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Already processed
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    if output_file.exists():

        print(
            f"SKIPPED: {json_file.name} "
            f"(already structured)"
        )

        return "skipped"


    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Load extracted JSON
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    data = load_json(
        json_file
    )


    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Only process successful extraction
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    if data.get("status") != "success":

        print(
            f"SKIPPED: {json_file.name} "
            f"(status={data.get('status')})"
        )

        return "skipped"


    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Check if document actually contains text
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    document_text = build_document_text(
        data
    )

    if len(document_text.strip()) < 50:

        print(
            f"SKIPPED: {json_file.name} "
            f"(very little extracted text)"
        )

        return "skipped"


    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Gemini
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    print(
        f"Sending to Gemini..."
    )


    structured_data = extract_experience(
        data
    )


    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Validate
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    valid, error = validate_experience(
        structured_data
    )

    if not valid:

        raise RuntimeError(
            error
        )


    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Preserve source metadata
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    structured_data["source"] = {

        "fileId": data.get(
            "fileId"
        ),

        "fileName": data.get(
            "fileName"
        ),

        **data.get(
            "source",
            {}
        )
    }


    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Save
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    with open(
        output_file,
        "w",
        encoding="utf-8"
    ) as file:

        json.dump(
            structured_data,
            file,
            ensure_ascii=False,
            indent=2
        )


    print(
        f"SUCCESS: {json_file.name}"
    )

    return "success"


# ============================================================
# MAIN
# ============================================================

def main():

    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Find ALL extracted JSON files
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    json_files = sorted(
        INPUT_DIR.glob("*.json")
    )


    print()
    print("=" * 60)
    print("INTERVJTI STRUCTURED INGESTION")
    print("=" * 60)

    print(
        f"Model       : {MODEL}"
    )

    print(
        f"Input files : {len(json_files)}"
    )

    print("=" * 60)
    print()


    if not json_files:

        print(
            "No extracted JSON files found."
        )

        return


    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Counters
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    successful = 0
    skipped = 0
    failed = 0


    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Process
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    for index, json_file in enumerate(
        json_files,
        start=1
    ):

        print(
            f"[{index}/{len(json_files)}] "
            f"{json_file.name}"
        )


        try:

            result = process_file(
                json_file
            )


            if result == "success":

                successful += 1

            elif result == "skipped":

                skipped += 1


        except Exception as error:

            failed += 1


            print(
                f"FAILED: {json_file.name}"
            )

            print(
                f"Error: {error}"
            )


            save_failure(
                json_file,
                error
            )


        print()


        # ----------------------------------------------------
        # Small delay to be friendly to free-tier limits
        # ----------------------------------------------------

        if index < len(json_files):

            time.sleep(1)


    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # FINAL SUMMARY
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    print()
    print("=" * 60)
    print("PROCESSING COMPLETE")
    print("=" * 60)

    print(
        f"Total input files : {len(json_files)}"
    )

    print(
        f"Successful        : {successful}"
    )

    print(
        f"Skipped           : {skipped}"
    )

    print(
        f"Failed            : {failed}"
    )

    print("=" * 60)


# ============================================================
# ENTRY POINT
# ============================================================

if __name__ == "__main__":

    main()

Optimal use of two power resources:\nTwo power resources and their initial power capacity were given as input. At every step we\nhave to optimally choose between one of the resources. At every step capacity of chosen\nresource gets reduced by 2 and that of the unchosen resource increases by 1 so you can only\nchoose a resource with capacity greater than 1. Repeat this until one of the power stations\ncapacity becomes zero.\nReturn the number of steps required if we use the resources optimally.\nSample input: 5, 3\nOutput: 6\nIt is solved by greedy approach by choosing the greater number at each step.\nI passed all test cases.\n2. Most similar string for a given query:\nGiven a list of strings and a query string, we have to find the string from the list which is most\nsimilar or closest to the given query string. To do so we have to calculate the Levenshtein\ndistance ( minimum number of insert a character/delete character / replace character\noperations to be performed on a string to convert the string to the given query). Return the\nword with lowest Levenshtein distance. If two words have the same Levenshtein distance,\nthen the a lexicographically smaller word is the answer.\nFinding the Levenshtein distance is a well known DP problem - Edit distance\nI partially passed test cases for this problem.\n3. Maximum Quirkiness (20 marks): \nGiven an array A of size N, find the pair of index {i,j} such that quirkiness between \nthem is maximum and return the maximum quirkiness. \nThe Quirkiness of two indexes i and j is defined as Q( i, j ) = Sum of array elements \nfrom index i to index j + constant*(j-i) \nQ(i,j) = ∑\n𝐴𝑛+ 𝑐(𝑗−𝑖)\n𝑗\n𝑛=𝑖\n \nWhere An is the sum of array elements from index i to j and j>i. \nAlso, indexing starts from 1 for the given array and the constant value was given. \nReturn the maximum quirkiness for the given array. \n \nExample: Consider N = 4, c=2, A= [4,1,2,-2] \nIf we take i=1,j=3 we get quirkiness = 7+ 2*(3-1) = 11 \nThis is the maximum quirkiness across all pairs of indexes. So, return 11. \n \nApproach:  \nI started with the brute force approach using three nested loops. One loop for \nchoosing ith index, another loop for choosing the jth index and third loop for \ncalculating the sum of array elements between i and j. So, using Kadane’s algorithm, I found out \nmaximum sum between any two indices and then found out the quirkiness for those \nindices and returned the value. A hero can \ndefeat a monster if his power is greater than or equal to the power of the monster. On \ndefeating a monster, the hero gains a certain amount of coins corresponding to that \nmonster. Return an array of N integers containing coins \nearned by each hero. The health of a hero doesn’t get reduced after defeating a \nmonster. There are r^2 pairs in \nthe worst case and time to calculate perfect divisor sum takes sqrt(r) time \n(assuming optimal algorithm which just checks till sqrt(n))]. Since r was <= 5 \n* 10^4 , it would take ~6 x 10^11 operations which is not feasible. (feasible \nshould mean <= 10^8). \n \nMy approach (while not the most optimal one) had time complexity r*sqrt(r) \n: ~10^7 operations, which worked. \nI iterated over the range (x=l+1, x<=r-1; x++) [or range(l+1, r) in python] and \nfor each number x in the range, I calculated the sum of perfect divisors (s). \nHence a possible y for this x is s - 1, as per the given condition. \nNow I calculated the sum of the perfect divisors of this y , and checked if it is \nequal to x+1. \nIf it is, then (x,y) is a valid pair. \n(I've left out some key edge cases here - see if you can identify them. I was a bit skeptical about my solution as I had only \nsolved the variation where we get the count of subarrays, not exact indices. \nBut in the end I provided the correct solution, with a short dry run and \npython code (code was not required).  \nI also thought of providing a sliding window approach, but time ran out and \nthat would not have worked for negative numbers anyways. \n \ndef subarraySumOneIndices(nums, k): \n    prefix_map = {0: -1} \n    prefix_sum = 0 \n \n    for i, num in enumerate(nums): \n        prefix_sum += num \n        if prefix_sum - k in prefix_map: \n            return (prefix_map[prefix_sum - k] + 1, i) \n        prefix_map[prefix_sum] = i \n \n    return None \n \nWhile writing the code I also mentioned python specific constructs, like how \na hashmap is declared in python, how we can’t use the ‘map’ keyword as it is \nreserved etc. (not needed at all, they just wanted the approach and dry run)"

He explained me what the question is: basically\nthere are 9 balls on a table and a weighing machine (not the digital one, one with two side\non which we can keep weights and compare the weights of two objects). one of the ball has\nslight different weight may be more or may be less, I have to find that ball from them using\nthat weighing machine. for example:\n1, 1.01, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1\ncan be the weights of 9 balls, I had no knowledge of this problem. First approach that I\ncame up with was to check each consecutive pairs in the weighing machine in order. (1, 2), (2,\n3) . . . there will be a moment when weighing machine show will deflection for two consecutive\npairs and we will find the second ball of first pair as answer. total of n operations has to be\nperformed (n = 9).\nSecond approach that I came up with was to compare each pair without intersection,\nselect the pair which shows deflection and compare the each ball of that pair with the\nremaining ball (9 th ball). If no pair shows the deflection 9 th ball is the answer. (1, 2), (3,\n4), (5, 6), (7, 8). the ball from odd pair which shows the deflection with last ball will be the\nanswer. this approach had n/2 operations.\nhe was still expecting more optimized, I finally understood it required the divide and\nconquer approach. we will weigh first 4 balls with last 4 balls, if there is no deflection,\nmiddle ball is answer. else seperate each 4 balls to 2-2 and weigh, the one which still shows\ndeflection that group contains the odd ball. This process had to be followed recursively.\nfinally comparing one ball of the final pair to remaining ball finding the answer. see the\nbelow steps\n 1 + 1.01 + 1 + 1 != 1 + 1 + 1 + 1\n 1 + 1.01 != 1 + 1 and 1 + 1 == 1 + 1\n 1 != 1.01 and 1 == 1\nhere we found the defective pair and now we compare one ball with remaining 1 ball,\nif we choose 1.01 randomly, weighing machine will shaw deflection. so it will be the\nanswer. If we choose 1, machine will show no deflection, therefore the other ball will\nbe answer.\nInterviewer was satisfied with my problem solving skills.\n10"

      "text": "VISA Experience \n   \n \n4\n2nd Question \nTeam Formation \n \nThe task was to form a team of size k from a given array by following below rules: \na) You need to take two windows of size w from front and rear side of the array. \nb) Take the greatest score from the both windows and add it to the answer variable, at last delete the \nconsidered score from the array (so that it is not taken into consideration for next iteration). \n \nSolution: \nI used a max heap and added all the elements that were present in the window of size (w + k), from front and \nrear side of the array. \nNow I just needed to pop the max heap k times. \n \n \nint helper(vector<int> score, int k, int w) \n{ \n    int n = score.size(); \n    priority_queue<int> q; \n    int ans = 0; \n    for (int i = 0; i < k + w; i++) \n    { \n        if (i < n) \n        { \n            q.push(score[i]); \n        } \n    } \n    for (int i = n - k - w; i < n; i++) \n    { \n        // this condition is to prevent adding elements from the front window so that we don’t overlap \n        if (i >= k + w) \n        { \n            q.push(score[i]); \n        } \n    } \n    for (int i = 0; i < k; i++) \n    { \n        ans += q.top(); \n        q.pop(); \n    } \n    return ans; \n} \n10/14 test cases were passed and I submitted with 20 mins remaining on the clock. \nAfter this round, 10 students were shortlisted."

Each piece is located in a single row and column and has four \nedges. Each edge comes in one of three types: inner, outer, and flat. A corner piece, for \nexample, will have two flat edges and two other edges, which could be inner or outer. \n \n \n \nAs we solve the jigsaw puzzle (manually or algorithmically), we'll need to store the \nposition of each piece. We could think about the position as absolute or relative: \n \n• \nAbsolute Position: \"This piece is located at position (12, 23).\" Absolute position \nwould belong to the Piece class itself and would include an orientation as well. \n• \nRelative Position: “I don’t know where this piece is actually located, but I know that it \nis next to this other piece.” The relative position would belong to the Edge class. \n \nFor our solution, we will use only the relative position, by adjoining edges to neighboring \nedges. \n \nA potential object-oriented design looks like the following: \n1 \nclass Edge { \n2 \n \nenum Type { inner, outer, flat } \n3 \n \nPiece parent; \n4 \n \nType type; \n5 \n \nint index; // Index into Piece.edges \n6 \n \nEdge attached_to; // Relative position \n7 \n8 \n \n/* See Algorithm section.       "text": "The solve method, implemented below, operates by picking an arbitrary start with. It \nthen finds an open edge on the corner and tries to match it to an open piece. When it \nfinds a match, it does the following: \n \n1. Attaches the edge. \n2. Removes the edge from the list of open edges. \n3. Finds the next open edge. \n \nThe next open edge is defined to be the one directly opposite the current edge, if it is \navailable. If it is not available, then the next edge can be any other edge. This will cause \nthe puzzle to be solved in a spiral-like fashion, from the outside to the inside. \n \nThe spiral comes from the fact that the algorithm always moves in a straight line, \nwhenever possible. When we reach the end of the first edge, the algorithm moves to the \nonly available edge on that corner piece—a 90-degree turn. It continues to take 90-\ndegree turns at the end of each side until the entire outer edge of the puzzle is \ncompleted. When that last edge piece is in place, that piece only has one exposed edge \nremaining, which is again a 90-degree turn. The algorithm repeats itself for subsequent \nrings around the puzzle, until finally all the pieces are in place. \n \nThis algorithm is implemented below with Java-like pseudocode. \n \n1 \npublic void solve() { \n2 \n \n/* Pick any corner to start with */ \n3 \n \nEdge currentEdge = getExposedEdge(corner[0]); \n4 \n5 \n \n/* Loop will iterate in a spiral like fashion until the puzzle \n6 \n \n* is full. */ \n7 \n \nwhile (currentEdge != null) { \n8 \n \n \n/* Match with opposite edges. You are required to calculate the minimum initial strength required by the robot to\ntravel from the source to reach the destination.\nNote :\n●\nA robot can only move one cell at a time, either down or right, i.e to cell (i+1,j) or\ncell (i,j+1) and it cannot move outside the matrix.\n●\nmat[0][0] = mat[m-1][n-1] = 0\nInput Format :\n●\nThe first line contains two space-separated integers i.e no of rows m and columns n\n●\nThe second line contains m*n integers separated by space (Elements of matrix)\nOutput Format :\nPrint the minimum initial strength required by the robot to travel from source to destination.\nThe question was similar to this one :\nhttps://www.geeksforgeeks.org/minimum-positive-points-to-reach-destination/\nI was successfully able to pass all the test cases for this problem.\n12 students were shortlisted for online interviews which were scheduled on MS teams."

The main \nobjective was to test profit-making skills based on a real-time demand-supply market scenario. \nTotal 38 candidates including me qualified for this round. 4 groups of 8-10 candidates were \nformed by them (Axxela). Trading simulation was carried-out within the group. There were 9 \nrounds; in each round a digit from a 9-digit number will be revealed. You have to quickly \ncalculate the minimum and maximum possible number i.e. determine the range based on the \nalready revealed digits and the remaining digits. Each digit from 0 to 9 will appear only once. \nWithin the range you have to predict the most likely value based on the prediction in the previous \nround. First round will be spontaneous but slowly it will converge to some range of value. You \nhave only 2 options “Buy” and “Sell”. On top right there will be a holdings section and total \ncount section. Total count can only range from -2 to +2. Holdings section will show at what price \nyou purchased. At any moment of time during the gameplay your aim should be to buy at the \nminimum possible price and sell at the maximum possible price so as to maximize the profit. All \nthis while staying closer to the probable true price or else closer to the most common bidding \nrange within the group. On your trading screen all the group member names and their buy/sell \nbid with price will be visible on which you have to keep a close eye as well as you have to keep \nin attention your holdings. A trade gets executed automatically whenever a buy and a sell order \ngets matched. My strategy was to neither buy more nor sell more so that I have both the options \nopen all the time according to the situation i.e keep holdings count in range (-1 to +1). Buying \nadds one to the count and selling subtracts one from the count. However if the deal favours profit \nyou can go to +2 or -2. I was not bidding for sell at very high price and waiting for it to be \nexecuted, which was done by most of the other candidates. I utilized something called as market \nmomentum i.e. keep less margin but execute more number of trades, following the broader trend \nvisible from available buy/sell bids. Because of this my total profit at the end of 9 rounds was \nsignificantly higher than others and I qualified for the Technical Interview round. In this round \nremember that the final score that will be displayed after 9 rounds will be different from the \nprofit that you’ve made because more points are awarded for trading close to average bidding \nrange and making profit rather than for bidding extraordinarily high or low.       "text": "2 \n \n \nOnline Assessment \nThe OA consisted of 4 DSA questions which were to be completed within 2 hours. \nThe questions were as follows: \n1. Redundancy Maximizer \nWe have been given a binary string servers where: \n'1' means a server is working. \n'0' means a server is redundant (backup). \nWe want to find the number of distinct possible counts of working servers after \noptimally flipping a contiguous segment of servers (i.e., changing '0' → '1' or '1' → '0'). \nExample 1 \nInput: servers = \"1100\" \nOriginal working servers = 2. \nFlip \"0\" → \"1\" → 3 working servers. \nFlip \"00\" → \"11\" → 4 working servers. \nFlip \"1\" → \"0\" → 1 working server. \nPossible counts = {1, 2, 3, 4} → Answer = 4 \nExample 2 \nInput: servers = \"111\" \nOriginal working = 3. \nFlipping any subarray decreases count. \nPossible counts = {1, 2, 3} → Answer = 3 \nApproach \nwhat I did was, I kind of treated this like Kadane’s algorithm (the max subarray sum thing). \nI thought of every '0' as a +1 (since flipping it gives me one more working server) and \nevery '1' as a -1 (since flipping it means I lose one working server). \nThen I just looked for the subarray that gives me the biggest gain, and also the one that \ngives me the biggest loss. Once I had those, I just added them to the original count of \nworking servers to figure out the minimum and maximum I could possibly get. \nFinally, the answer is just the range of values from that minimum to that maximum. \n \n2. Optimal Team Size \nWe are given n players. For each player, we have: \nlowerSkill[i]: minimum skill position they can play. \nhigherSkill[i]: maximum skill position they can play. \nWe want to find the largest possible team size we can form, such that for each position \nfrom 0 to teamSize-1, some player can fit there (within their skill range). \nExample 1 \nInput: \nlowerSkill = [0, 1, 2] \nhigherSkill = [2, 2, 2] \n \nWe can form team of size 3 because:"
    },

      "pageNumber": 3,
      "text": "3 \n \nPlayer 1 fits position 0 \nPlayer 2 fits position 1 \nPlayer 3 fits position 2 \nAnswer = 3 \nExample 2 \nInput: \nlowerSkill = [0, 0, 1] \nhigherSkill = [1, 2, 2] \nMax possible team size = 2 \n(cannot place 3 players because constraints won’t match) \nAnswer = 2 \nApproach \njust used Binary Search on the possible team size. \nFor each mid value, I checked if it’s actually possible to form a team of that size using a \ngreedy method (I called it canFormTeam). \nIf it worked, then I moved the search to the right (trying for a bigger team). \nIf it didn’t work, I moved left (settling for a smaller team). \n \n3.       "text": "Sidenote:\nMaximum Index - My approach\nOkay, so if you did find an approach, great! But don’t worry if you did not…\nLet’s look at my observations and approach.\nObservation\nI looked at the examples and figured out 2 things:\n1.\nThe aim is to maximize the final index.\n2. A step means either to “stay” at the same index or “move on”.\n3. The leap I can take increases with each step.\n(At the 5th step my leap is of 5 indexes)\n4. I cannot take a leap in which I encounter the bad index/bad element.\nApproach\nLet’s forget about the bad index for a second and just focus on the step choice.\nI figured that I should aim to always choose to “move on” when at a higher index,\notherwise I will miss out on the opportunity of taking a giant leap.\nWhat this means is, IF I want to “stay” I should prefer to “stay” early on in the game rather\nthan later, otherwise I will miss out on a giant leap later on.\nExample:\nInitially i=0, j=1 (according to problem statement)\n●\nI choose to stay at 0, and j counter increases to 2 now.\n●\nI choose to stay at 0, and the j counter increases to 3 now.\n●\nI choose to stay at 0 again and the j counter increases to 4 now.\nObserve that with each choice/step, the value of j increases, and I am missing out on an\nopportunity to jump ‘j’ number of steps.\nSo I should choose to “stay” only at the initial stage of the game where the stakes are low\nand my leap value is least (this happens when i=0, j=1).\nWe want to keep leaping in order to maximize the final landing index.\nOkay so one major thing out of the way, I should “stay” ONLY IF i=0, j=1. Otherwise I won’t\nbe maximizing the final index.\nSo what about the bad index/bad element? I want to avoid leaping onto the bad index at"
    },
    {
      "pageNumber": 9,
      "text": "any step. I can avoid this easily. Notice in the example:\nsteps = 4\nbadElement = 6\nThe pointer is limited to 4 steps and should avoid the bad item 6.\n●\nScenario 1:\n○\nIn the first step, j starts at 1.\n○\nMove 1 unit to index 0+1=1 and j=2.\n○\nAt step 2, move 2 units to index 1+2-3, and j=3.\n○\nAt step 3, do not move. Otherwise point moves 3 units to bad item 6. Now j=4.\n○\nAt step 4, move 4 units to item 3+4=7.\n●\nScenario 2:\n○\nAt step 1, remain at index 0. Now j=2.\n○\nAt step 2, move 2 units to index 0+2-2 and j=3.\n○\nAt step 3, move 3 units to index 2+3=5 and j=4\n○\nAt step 4, move 4 units to index 5+4=9\nThe maximum index that can be reached is 9.\nIn scenario 1:\nWe chose to move at step 1 itself. Then we choose to not move at step 3 since we’ll\nencounter the bad element, thus missing out on a leap of 3 units. 0->1->3->(stay)->3->7\nIn scenario 2:\nWhat if we chose to not move at step 1 itself? Now j=2.\nObviously we won’t encounter the bad index=6 now, because the leap distance has\nchanged by 1 for each step and thus we will be off by one unit.\nSo now if we keep leaping: 0->(stay)->2->5->9.\nSo all you have to do is, find out:\nmax ( final index when leap at step 1, final index when stay at step 1 )\n( Final index when stay at step 1 will be ) > ( Final index when leap at step 1 )\nONLY if the bad index lies in the path of ( Final index when leap at step 1 ) and the reverse\nis also true."

      "text": "1. Minimum servers with maximum load:\nIt took me ten to fifteen minutes to figure out the solution. I was able to complete\nevery test case. To be honest, it was a greedy problem that could be solved with\nsome observation and insight rather than any knowledge of DSA. Try it out before\nreading my method.\nI was given the projected load and vector capacity of 'n' servers.\nI have to find out how many servers are needed to handle the anticipated load.\nThe bare minimum of severs should be used.\nMy Approach:\nThe question was quite simple, but in an attempt to mislead the candidate, a very\nlong description was provided. However, based on my observations, I discovered\nthat it is really just a greed issue, similar to the knapsack dilemma.\nSo I first sort the severs array in ascending order and then start the loop from the\nback of the array. Each time I check if current server capacity is smaller than or\nequal to current expected load or if expected load - current server capacity is >=\n0 to ensure we are choosing correct server. If any of these conditions are met\nthen we decrement that server capacity from the expected load & increment the\ncounter to keep track of the servers used.\nExplanation with Eg:\nInput:\nservers = [4, 12, 10, 14, 6]\nexpected_load = 32\nOutput:\n3\nIn this case, after sorting, the array will look like: [4, 6, 10, 12, 14]\nNow we start from the last element of array so\nfirst we take 14, hence 32 - 14 = 18\nThen we take 12 as it is <= 18, 18 - 12 = 6\nNow we skip 10 as it is > 6\nAt last we take 6."

Each hen will peck at least once, either \nthe hen to its right or left. Find the maximum number of hens that remain unpecked. \n \nThe Hen Puzzle — Solution \nA hen remains unpecked only when both neighbours peck away from it. So think in groups of 3 \n— the unpecked hen sits in the middle with the two on either side pecking outward. 100 ÷ 3 = \n33. I didn't get it immediately, and the interviewer did help me through it — don't be afraid to \nthink out loud and ask help. \n \nOne important thing to note was that the interview was actually built around my OA \nperformance; they had a full analysis showing strengths and weaknesses, and my maths and \nfinancials clearly outshone my coding which shaped the direction of questions."

(Go through the projects you make once before the\ninterviews )\n●Then the interviewer asked me to rate myself in terms of coding.\nSo I told him 8 out of 10.\n●Then he started asking me DSA questions 🙂:\n1) Given an array of integers nums and an integer k, return\ntotal number of subarrays whose sum is equal to k.\nSample Input 1: nums=[1,1,1], k=2\nSample Output 1 : 2\nExplanation : There are 2 subarrays - one from index 0 to\nindex 1 ({1,1}) and another from index 1 to index 2 ({1,1})\nwhose sum is 2.\nSample Input 2 : nums=[1,2,3], k=3\nSample Output 2 : 2\nExplanation : There are 2 subarrays -  one from index 0 to\nindex 1({1,2}) and another is just index 2 ({3}).\nSo I started giving the Brute Force solution - Find all the\nsubarrays using two nested for loops and then calculate\nthe sum for each subarray. The subarray whose sum is\nequal to k will be included in the final answer.\nHe asked me about the time and space complexity of the\nsolution so it was O(n^2) in terms of time and O(1) in terms\nof space.\nThe above brute force approach was correct. But then he\ntold me to optimize the solution. So what I did is to use the\nmethod similar to the problem - (Find the number of\nsubarrays whose sum is 0).\nI explained to him how the above optimized solution will\nwork and also wrote the code for the above problem.\nint subarraySum(vector<int>& nums, int k) {\nint sum=0;\nint ans=0;\nunordered_map<int,int> u;\nu[0]=1;\nfor(int i=0;i<int(nums.size());i++){\nsum=sum+nums[i];\nans=ans+u[sum-k];\nu[sum]++;\n}\nreturn ans;\n}\nThen he asked me about the time and space complexity\nwhich was both equal to O(n)\n2) Given the group of integers and the  integer k, find the\nlargest integer in the group which is smaller than k\nSo I told him that, we will maintain the answer variable\ninitialized to some min_value(INT_MIN) and then we will\niterate through the numbers and then we will change this\nanswer variable only when nums[i] < k  && nums[i] > answer\nSo suppose the numbers was {2, 5, 9, 11, 6} and k=8\nThen answer = INT_MIN\nFor i=0;\nnums[0] < k && nums[0]>answer, so answer=nums[0]\nSo answer=2\nFor i=1;\nnums[1] < k && nums[1]>answer, so answer=nums[1]\nSo answer=5\nFor i=2;\nnums[2] !< k , so no change\nFor i=3;\nnums[3]  !< k, so no change\nFor i=4\nnums[4] < k && nums[4] >answer, so answer=nums[4]\nSo answer=6\nWhich is correct.\nThe  time complexity of this solution was O(n)\nBut then he told me to optimize this approach.\nThen I was a bit confused about how to further reduce the\ncomplexity. So then I thought of an algorithm like binary\nsearch because the time complexity less than O(n) is O(log\nn).\nBut to apply something like binary search, we need an\narray in a sorted manner. So I told the interviewer that the\nalgo can be something like binary search but we need to\nfirst sort the array. But in that case the complexity will\nincrease to O(n log n). Then he told me that he never\nmentioned the group of integers in the array. Then the first\nthing that came to my mind was SET. We will take the\ninput in SET which will keep the integers in the sorted\nmanner and then we can apply algorithms like binary\nsearch.But then too we need to insert the element into the\nset which will be taking O(n log n) time complexity. But\nthen he mentioned that the time complexity of the input\nwill not be considered. So then  the task was simple.\nTake the Integers into SET whose time complexity will not\nby considered and then just apply the algo like binary\nsearch and then the complexity will be O(log n).\nInterviewer didn’t ask me how I would implement that\nBinary search algo. What he asked me is the difference\nbetween a hash set and a tree set. This was the only\nquestion I wasn't able to answer🤢.
